newsitem.title: PERU: Peru bus plunges into ravine, 40 presumed dead.
newsitem.headline: Peru bus plunges into ravine, 40 presumed dead.

text.p: A bus plunged into a ravine early on Tuesday in the Peruvian Andes killing at least 28 passengers with another 12 presumed dead, officials said.

"It appears around 40 are dead. The figure is unofficial because rescue operations are still going on," said local fire chief Luis Guevara, who had been coordinating the search for possible survivors since the accident occurred just after midnight.
The bus carrying around 70 passengers hurtled off the mountain highway at Carpatata 200 miles (320 km) northeast of Lima and plummeted about 100 yards (100 meters), Guevara said.

Officials at the Feliz Mayorca Soto hospital, which was handling the emergency, said by mid-morning they had received 28 corpses and 32 injured passengers. They did not expect to see more survivors from the crash.
"It has been hours since we took in anybody injured in the crash," nurse Zoraya Vargas said. "We only expect corpses now."
Authorities said they did know the cause of the crash that occurred as the bus was snaking through the mountains from Satipo to Tarma in the northern department of San Martin.

The frequency of road accidents in the Peruvian Andes, where most people travel along poorly maintained highways on buses that are often overloaded, has led opposition parties to call for stricter transport regulations.
